title: Don't let our hearts swerve
hook: our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You guided us (3:8)

segments.voice: Yesterday: muhkam, the firm verses, the mother of the Book, and your line, some verses are for sitting with.

Yesterday's verse carried a warning: some have a swerve in their hearts, and chase what's unclear. The very next verse doesn't point a finger at them. It turns around and asks for help. Commentators hear the people just praised, those firmly rooted in knowledge, as the ones speaking. Their first worry isn't other people's hearts. It's their own. If anyone could feel safe from drifting, it's them. They don't.
screen: `A SWERVE IN THE HEART.` → `THE NEXT VERSE TURNS AROUND.` → `NOT THEIR HEARTS. OURS.`

segments.voice: In Pickthall's translation, 3:8 begins: "Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us." Then it asks for mercy from God's own presence, and ends: You are the Bestower. Notice the link. Yesterday's verse said zaygh, a swerve, in the hearts of some. Today's asks la tuzigh, don't let them swerve. Same root, z-y-gh: to lean, to tilt away from straight. One verse describes the tilt; the next asks to be kept from it. Notice the timing too: after You guided us. It's a prayer for people who've already found the way and know that finding it once isn't the same as staying on it. A hadith in Tirmidhi reports that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ often said: O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon your religion. Anas, who reports it, says the companions asked whether he feared for them, and he said yes: hearts are held between two of God's fingers, and He turns them as He wills. Turner of hearts is muqallib al-qulub, and both words share one root, q-l-b, to turn over: the heart is named as the thing that turns. Some Muslims say 3:8 in their supplications after the prayer. And it closes a week about keeping things: a man raised after a hundred years, a grain that multiplies, a gift unspoiled, a debt written down, a burden that fits, verses held firm or held open. Today, a heart kept straight.
screen: `THE SWERVE, AND THE REQUEST` · `Z-Y-GH: TO TILT AWAY` · `AFTER YOU GUIDED US` · `QALB: THE THING THAT TURNS` · then, large: `OUR LORD! CAUSE NOT OUR HEARTS TO STRAY.`

segments.voice: Sit up straight and feel how small the movements are that keep you upright, a lean forward, a correction back; nobody sits perfectly still. Think of one place this week where your heart tilted a little, toward impatience, envy or carelessness, and without scolding it, notice the lean and come back to center. If you pray, you can say 3:8 in Arabic or your own language: rabbana la tuzigh qulubana.
Zaygh, a swerve in the heart. The request of 3:8, la tuzigh, asks not to let it happen, made by people already guided, who want to stay that way. Today's word.
Your line: keep my heart straight. A lean you notice is a lean you can correct. That's a week, done.

howItsDone: Many Muslims say the supplication of 3:8, 'rabbana la tuzigh qulubana', after the daily prayers and in personal du'a, along with the Prophet's reported prayer to the Turner of hearts.

options: 3:8 is asked after guidance: finding the way isn't the same as staying on it.
Because they doubt they were ever truly guided in the first place.
It's only a prayer for people who have already left the faith.
